scenes.title: IS NULL
scenes.narration: IS NULL is the correct way to test for missing values, since NULL never equals anything.

scenes.title: Handling missing data
bullets: NULL means unknown, not zero or empty
Use IS NULL and IS NOT NULL instead
scenes.narration: NULL represents an unknown or missing value, which is different from zero or an empty string. Because NULL is not equal to anything, even to another NULL, ordinary comparisons never match it. The dedicated IS NULL and IS NOT NULL operators are how you test for it reliably.

scenes.title: Finding missing values
scenes.narration: This query looks for customers who have no phone number recorded. Using IS NULL correctly catches those missing entries. The result lists every customer whose phone field was never filled in.

scenes.heading: = NULL vs IS NULL
scenes.narration: Writing a column equals NULL never works, because comparing to NULL yields unknown rather than true. As a result, that expression matches no rows at all. IS NULL is the purpose-built operator that correctly identifies missing values.

scenes.text: Always use IS NULL and IS NOT NULL to handle missing data correctly.
scenes.narration: Test for missing data with IS NULL and IS NOT NULL, never with an equals sign, since NULL comparisons always resolve to unknown.
